title: The boat pits as acid-filled circuit breakers
summary: Geoffrey Drumm tells of The boat pits as acid-filled circuit breakers, about dynastic Egypt; recent analysis at Egypt (no place named), and says they saw it or took part. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: So inside the boat pits adjacent to the Great Pyramid, we find more sulfate compounds.

plain: Geoffrey Drumm, who studies the pyramids of Egypt, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that the boat pits, long trenches cut into the rock beside the Great Pyramid at Giza, contain more sulfate compounds, chemicals linked to acid. He believes the pits were filled with acid and worked like circuit breakers, devices that cut off electricity when it surges. If true, it would mean the Great Pyramid was some kind of power machine.
